note: Accepted boundary violations as of 2026-09-07, the day before the three extractions land. Every row is a real coupling that the guard would otherwise fail on; each names the extraction expected to remove it. Rules: nothing may be added here to make a new violation pass without a reviewed reason; a row whose violation no longer exists is a hard failure in --mode enforce, so a fix must delete its row in the same commit. Regenerate the mechanical parts with `--write-baseline`, which preserves removed_by and why and leaves new rows as "unassigned" (also a hard failure), then attribute them by hand.

The coordinator binds to substrate internals rather than a published surface: core.endpoint.resolve_endpoint, core.shell_ops.remote_bash, and the source text of .remote-dev/core/managed_jobs.py, which it compiles and execs on the remote host. remote-dev has to publish an endpoint resolver, a bash entry point and a managed-job worker before this can be rewired — which is why remote-dev's extraction has to settle before the coordinator's.

The parity denylist hard-codes .remote-dev/state/ so the substrate's state is never synced to a remote container. Correct behaviour, wrong source of truth: remote-dev should publish the paths a host application must exclude.

The headline reverse dependency. Managed machine/session resolution puts .agents/lib on sys.path and imports the scaffold's resolve_remote_target, and the selector-less branch falls through to that same path so a bare remote.bash auto-binds to the nearest session worktree. The substrate must accept an injected resolver from its host application instead of importing one.
